```javascript
    const fractionalRemainders = [];
    const originalIndices = [];

        const baseAmount = Math.floor(budget * weight / totalWeight);
        const fractionalRemainder = (budget * weight) % totalWeight;
        
        baseAllocations.push(baseAmount);
        fractionalRemainders.push(fractionalRemainder);
        originalIndices.push(i);

    // Create list of indices sorted by fractional remainder (descending), ties go to earlier index
    const sortedIndices = originalIndices.slice().sort((a, b) => {
        if (fractionalRemainders[b] !== fractionalRemainders[a]) {
            return fractionalRemainders[b] - fractionalRemainders[a];
        }
        return a - b; // Earlier request comes first on tie

    let remainingBudget = budget;
    for (let i = 0; i < requests.length; i++) {

    let remainingToDistribute = remainingBudget;

        sortedIndices.shift();

        if (remainingToDistribute === 0) break;

    // Return results in original order
    return requests.map((req, i) => ({ name: req.name, amount: baseAllocations[i] }));
```

```typescript
export class MinHeap {
  private heap: number[];

  constructor() {
    this.heap = [];
  }

  private bubbleUp(index: number): void {
    while (index > 0) {
      const parentIndex = Math.floor((index - 1) / 2);
      if (this.heap[index] < this.heap[parentIndex]) {
        [this.heap[index], this.heap[parentIndex]] = [this.heap[parentIndex], this.heap[index]];
        index = parentIndex;
      } else {
        break;
      }
    }
  }

  private bubbleDown(index: number): void {
    const length = this.heap.length;
    while (true) {
      const leftChildIndex = 2 * index + 1;
      const rightChildIndex = 2 * index + 2;
      let smallestIndex = index;

      if (leftChildIndex < length && this.heap[leftChildIndex] < this.heap[smallestIndex]) {
        smallestIndex = leftChildIndex;
      }
      if (rightChildIndex < length && this.heap[rightChildIndex] < this.heap[smallestIndex]) {
        smallestIndex = rightChildIndex;
      }
      if (smallestIndex === index) {
        break;
      }
      [this.heap[index], this.heap[smallestIndex]] = [this.heap[smallestIndex], this.heap[index]];
      index = smallestIndex;
    }
  }

  push(value: number): void {
    this.heap.push(value);
    const index = this.heap.length - 1;
    this.bubbleUp(index);
  }

  pop(): number | undefined {
    if (this.heap.length === 0) {
      return undefined;
    }
    if (this.heap.length === 1) {
      return this.heap.pop()!;
    }
    const root = this.heap[0];
    this.heap[0] = this.heap.pop()!;
    this.bubbleDown(0);
    return root;
  }

  peek(): number | undefined {
    if (this.heap.length === 0) {
      return undefined;
    }
    return this.heap[0];
  }

  size(): number {
    return this.heap.length;
  }

  toArray(): number[] {
    return [...this.heap];
  }
}
```

The standard recurrence relation is:

- If a[i-1] == b[j-1]: dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j-1]

  - dp[i][j-1]: insertion into a

```cpp
#include <algorithm>
#include <vector>

int editDistance(const std::string& a, const std::string& b) {
    size_t n = a.size();
    size_t m = b.size();
    
    // Use the shorter string to minimize space
    size_t len = std::min(n, m);
    std::vector<int> prev(len + 1, 0);
    std::vector<int> curr(len + 1, 0);
    
    // Initialize first row
    for (int j = 0; j <= len; j++) {
        prev[j] = j;
    }

    for (int i = 1; i <= (n > m ? n : m); i++) {
        for (int j = 1; j <= len; j++) {
            if (a[i - 1] == b[j - 1]) {
                curr[j] = prev[j - 1];
            } else {
                curr[j] = 1 + std::min({prev[j - 1], prev[j], curr[j - 1]});
            }
        }
        // Swap rows
        std::swap(prev, curr);
    }
    
    return prev[len];
}
```

```cpp
std::vector<int> nextGreater(const std::vector<int>& values) {
    std::vector<int> result(values.size(), -1);

    for (int i = 0; i < values.size(); ++i) {
        while (!stack.empty() && values[stack.top()] < values[i]) {
            int topIndex = stack.top();
            stack.pop();
            result[topIndex] = values[i];
        }
        stack.push(i);
```

```python
    n = len(s)
    max_len = 0
```

```python
def column_number(label: str) -> int:
    """Convert an uppercase spreadsheet column label to its 1-based integer value.
    
    Args:
        label: Uppercase string like "A", "Z", "AB", etc.
        
    Returns:

    Raises:
        ValueError: If label is empty or contains non-A..Z characters.
    """

        raise ValueError("Label cannot be empty")
    
    if not label.isupper():
        raise ValueError("Label must contain only uppercase letters A-Z")
    
    char_values = {chr(ord('A') + i): i + 1 for i in range(26)}
    
    result = 0
    for char in label:
        if char not in char_values:
            raise ValueError(f"Invalid character '{char}' in label")
        result = result * 26 + char_values[char]
    
    return result


def column_label(n: int) -> str:
    """Convert a positive integer to its spreadsheet column label.
    
    Args:
        n: Positive integer.
        
    Returns:
        The uppercase column label.
        
    Raises:
        ValueError: If n <= 0.
    """
    if n <= 0:
        raise ValueError("Column number must be positive")
    
    result = []
    while n > 0:
        n -= 1  # Convert to 0-indexed for modulo
        remainder = n % 26
        result.append(chr(ord('A') + remainder))
        n //= 26
    
    return ''.join(reversed(result))
```

```cpp
int lcsLength(const std::string& a, const std::string& b) {
    int n = a.length();
    int m = b.length();
    
    // Create DP table with rolling rows
    // We need m+1 columns (0 to m)
    std::vector<int> dp(m + 1, 0);
    
    // Previous row (initially all zeros)
    for (int j = 0; j <= m; ++j) {
        dp[j] = 0;
    }
    
    for (int i = 1; i <= n; ++i) {
        std::vector<int> new_dp(m + 1, 0);
        for (int j = 1; j <= m; ++j) {
            if (a[i - 1] == b[j - 1]) {
                new_dp[j] = dp[j - 1] + 1;
            } else {
                new_dp[j] = std::max(dp[j], new_dp[j - 1]);
            }
        }
        dp = std::move(new_dp);
    }
    
    return dp[m];
}
```

```typescript
class BoundedCache<V> {
    private maxSize: number;
    private entries: Map<string, V>;
    private order: string[]; // tracks insertion order

    constructor(maxSize: number) {

            this.maxSize = 0;
            this.entries = new Map();
            this.order = [];
        } else {
            this.maxSize = maxSize;
            this.entries = new Map();
            this.order = [];
        }

        if (this.maxSize <= 0) {
            return;
        }

        if (this.entries.has(key)) {
            // Update existing key - keep original position
            this.entries.set(key, value);
        } else {
            // New key
            if (this.entries.size >= this.maxSize) {
                // Evict oldest (first in order array)
                const oldestKey = this.order.shift() as string;
                this.entries.delete(oldestKey);
            }
            this.entries.set(key, value);
            this.order.push(key);
        }

        return this.entries.get(key);
    }

    has(key: string): boolean {

            return false;
        }
        this.entries.delete(key);
        const index = this.order.indexOf(key);
        if (index !== -1) {
            this.order.splice(index, 1);
        }
        return true;
    }

    size(): number {
        return this.entries.size;
    }

    keys(): string[] {
        return [...this.order];
    }
}
```

```python
def palindrome_cuts(s: str) -> int:
    n = len(s)
    if n <= 1:
        return 0
    
    # dp[i] = minimum cuts needed for s[:i]
    dp = [float('inf')] * (n + 1)
    dp[0] = 0
    
    # Precompute palindrome table
    is_palindrome = [[False] * n for _ in range(n)]
    for length in range(1, n + 1):
        for i in range(n - length + 1):
            j = i + length - 1
            if length == 1:
                is_palindrome[i][j] = True
            elif length == 2:
                is_palindrome[i][j] = s[i] == s[j]
            else:
                is_palindrome[i][j] = (s[i] == s[j]) and is_palindrome[i + 1][j - 1]
    
    for i in range(1, n + 1):
        # Initial worst case: each char is a palindrome, i-1 cuts total
        dp[i] = i - 1
        for j in range(i):
            if is_palindrome[j][i - 1]:
                dp[i] = min(dp[i], dp[j] + (0 if j == 0 else 1))
    
    return dp[n]
```

```python
import math

def quantile(values, q):
    if not values:
        raise ValueError("Empty sequence")
    if q < 0 or q > 1:
        raise ValueError("q must be in [0, 1]")
    
    sorted_values = sorted(values)
    n = len(sorted_values)
    position = q * (n - 1)
    lower_idx = int(math.floor(position))
    upper_idx = lower_idx + 1
    fractional_part = position - lower_idx
    
    if upper_idx >= n:
        return float(sorted_values[n - 1])
    
    return float(sorted_values[lower_idx] + fractional_part * (sorted_values[upper_idx] - sorted_values[lower_idx]))
```

```cpp
    if (grid.empty() || grid[0].empty()) {
        return 0;
    }

    int n = grid[0].size();
    
    // Use DP table
    std::vector<std::vector<int>> dp(m, std::vector<int>(n, 0));
    
    // Base case: starting cell
    dp[0][0] = grid[0][0];
    
    // Fill first row (can only come from left)
    for (int j = 1; j < n; j++) {
        dp[0][j] = dp[0][j-1] + grid[0][j];
    }
    
    // Fill first column (can only come from above)
    for (int i = 1; i < m; i++) {
        dp[i][0] = dp[i-1][0] + grid[i][0];

    // Fill the rest of the DP table
    for (int i = 1; i < m; i++) {
        for (int j = 1; j < n; j++) {
            dp[i][j] = grid[i][j] + std::min(dp[i-1][j], dp[i][j-1]);
        }
    }
    
    return dp[m-1][n-1];
```

```python
    line1 = sys.stdin.readline().split()
    n = int(line1[0])
    k = int(line1[1])
    
    # Read the n integers from the second line

    window_sum = sum(arr[:k])
    max_sum = window_sum
    
    # Slide the window across the array

        # Remove the element that is no longer in the window
        # Add the new element that has entered the window
        window_sum = window_sum - arr[i - k] + arr[i]
        # Update the maximum sum found so far

            max_sum = window_sum
    
    # Output the result
    print(max_sum)

if __name__ == "__main__":
```

```python
    else:
```

```python
def next_permutation(values: list[int]) -> list[int]:
    """Return the next lexicographically greater permutation of the input list.
    If the sequence is the last permutation (descending), wrap to ascending order."""
    
    # Create a copy to avoid modifying the input
    result = values.copy()
    
    n = len(result)
    if n <= 1:
        return result
    
    # Step 1: Find the largest index k such that result[k] < result[k + 1]
    k = n - 2
    while k >= 0 and result[k] >= result[k + 1]:
        k -= 1
    
    if k < 0:
        # The list is in descending order - reverse to get ascending (wrap)
        result.reverse()
        return result
    
    # Step 2: Find the largest index l > k such that result[k] < result[l]
    l = n - 1
    while result[l] <= result[k]:
        l -= 1
    
    # Step 3: Swap result[k] with result[l]
    result[k], result[l] = result[l], result[k]
    
    # Step 4: Reverse elements from k + 1 to the end
    result[k + 1:] = result[k + 1:][::-1]
```

```python
def count_product_less(values: list[int], limit: int) -> int:
    if limit <= 1:
        return 0
    
    n = len(values)
    if n == 0:
        return 0
    
    left = 0
    product = 1
    count = 0
    
    for right in range(n):
        # Expand window to include values[right]
        product *= values[right]
        
        # Shrink window from left while product >= limit
        while product >= limit:
            product //= values[left]
            left += 1
        
        # All subarrays ending at right from left to right are valid
        count += (right - left + 1)
    
    return count
```

```cpp
        auto& intervalA = a[i];
        auto& intervalB = b[j];
        
        int start = std::max(intervalA.first, intervalB.first);
        int end = std::min(intervalA.second, intervalB.second);

        } else {

        }

    return result;
```

```typescript
  const result: [string, T][] = [];

    }
  }

  const result: Record<string, T> = {};
  for (const [key, value] of pairs) {
```

```typescript
    if (value === null || typeof value !== 'object') {

            errors.push(key);

    Object.keys(schema).forEach(key => {

        if (!Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(value, key)) {
            errors.push(key);

        if (valueField === null) {
            errors.push(key);

        // Validate type

                    errors.push(key);
                }
                break;
        }
    });
```

3. For each position i:

```cpp
            z[i] = std::min(R - i + 1, z[i - L]);
        }
        
        while (i + z[i] < n && s[z[i]] == s[i + z[i]]) {
```

```python
def group_anagrams(words):
    if not words:
        return []
    
    from collections import defaultdict
    
    # Group words by their sorted character representation
    anagram_groups = defaultdict(list)
    for word in words:
        sorted_word = ''.join(sorted(word.lower()))
        anagram_groups[sorted_word].append(word)
    
    # Convert to list of groups, sort each group alphabetically
    groups = []
    for key in anagram_groups:
        groups.append(sorted(anagram_groups[key]))
    
    # Sort groups by their first word
    groups.sort(key=lambda group: group[0] if group else '')
    
    return groups
```

```python
def multi_key_sort(records, keys):
    """
    Sort a list of dicts by multiple keys.

    Args:
        records: List of dictionaries to sort
        keys: List of (field, descending) tuples, most significant first

    Returns:
        A NEW sorted list without modifying input or dicts.
    """
    def sort_key(record):
        key_values = []
        for field, descending in keys:
            value = record.get(field)
            if descending:
                # For descending numeric values, negate them
                if isinstance(value, (int, float)) and not isinstance(value, bool):
                    value = -value
            key_values.append(value)
        return tuple(key_values)
    
    return sorted(records, key=sort_key)
```

```python
from collections import deque

def tree_diameter(edges):
    """
    Returns the number of edges on the longest path of a tree.
    Uses two BFS passes to find the diameter in O(V) time.
    
    Args:
        edges: List of (u, v) tuples representing undirected edges
        
    Returns:
        int: Number of edges on the longest path (tree diameter)
        
    Raises:
        ValueError: If input represents a disconnected graph
    """
    # Handle edge case: no edges means single or zero nodes
    if not edges:
        return 0
    
    # Build adjacency list and collect all nodes
    adj = {}
    nodes = set()
    
    for u, v in edges:
        if u not in adj:
            adj[u] = []
        if v not in adj:
            adj[v] = []
        adj[u].append(v)
        adj[v].append(u)
        nodes.add(u)
        nodes.add(v)
    
    # If no nodes, return 0
    if not nodes:
        return 0
    
    # Check if number of edges matches tree requirement (V - 1 edges for V nodes)
    if len(edges) != len(nodes) - 1:
        raise ValueError("Input is not a valid tree structure")
    
    # Verify all nodes are connected using BFS
    visited = set()
    queue = deque()
    queue.append(list(nodes)[0])
    visited.add(list(nodes)[0])
    
    while queue:
        node = queue.popleft()
        if node in adj:
            for neighbor in adj[node]:
                if neighbor not in visited:
                    visited.add(neighbor)
                    queue.append(neighbor)
    
    if len(visited) != len(nodes):
        raise ValueError("Disconnected input")
    
    # First BFS from arbitrary node to find farthest node
    start_node = list(nodes)[0]
    distances = {start_node: 0}
    queue = deque([start_node])
    
    while queue:
        node = queue.popleft()
        for neighbor in adj[node]:
            if neighbor not in distances:
                distances[neighbor] = distances[node] + 1
                queue.append(neighbor)
    
    # Find the farthest node from start_node
    farthest_node = max(distances, key=distances.get)
    
    # Second BFS from farthest node to find actual diameter
    distances = {farthest_node: 0}
    queue = deque([farthest_node])
    
    while queue:
        node = queue.popleft()
        for neighbor in adj[node]:
            if neighbor not in distances:
                distances[neighbor] = distances[node] + 1
                queue.append(neighbor)
```

```python
def glob_match(pattern, text):

            elif pattern[i - 1] == text[j - 1]:
```

```javascript
function roundRobin(tasks, quantum) {
  if (quantum < 1) {
    throw new RangeError('quantum must be >= 1');
  }
  
  // Create a copy of tasks to avoid modifying original
  let queue = [...tasks];
  let result = [];
  let totalTime = 0;
  
  // Process queue until empty
  while (queue.length > 0) {
    let task = queue.shift();
    
    // Skip tasks with time <= 0

    let runTime = Math.min(quantum, task.time);
    task.time -= runTime;

    if (task.time > 0) {
      queue.push(task);
    }
  }
```

```cpp
int lisLength(const std::vector<int>& values) {
    std::vector<int> tails;
    // Optimization: reserve memory to avoid reallocations
    if (!values.empty()) {
        tails.reserve(values.size());
    }

    for (int x : values) {
        // Use lower_bound to find the first element in tails that is >= x.
        // This works for strictly increasing subsequences:
        // If x is greater than all tails, it extends the longest subsequence found so far.
        // If x is less than or equal to some tail, replacing it maintains the smallest tail
        // for that length, allowing longer subsequences to be formed later.
        auto it = std::lower_bound(tails.begin(), tails.end(), x);
        
        if (it == tails.end()) {
            tails.push_back(x);
        } else {
            *it = x;
        }
    }
    return static_cast<int>(tails.size());
```

```javascript
  if (typeof p !== 'number' || isNaN(p) || p < 0 || p > 100) {
    throw new RangeError('p must be between 0 and 100');
  }
  
  // Validate input array
  if (!Array.isArray(values) || values.length === 0) {
    throw new RangeError('Empty array');
  }
  
  // Check for non-finite values
  for (let i = 0; i < values.length; i++) {
    if (!isFinite(values[i])) {
      throw new TypeError('Non-finite values not allowed');
    }
  }
  
  // Make a copy to avoid sorting in place
  const sorted = [...values].sort((a, b) => a - b);
  const n = sorted.length;
  
  // Calculate rank using formula: rank = p / 100 * (n - 1)
  const rank = (p / 100) * (n - 1);
  
  // Get the lower and upper indices
  const lowerIdx = Math.floor(rank);
  const upperIdx = Math.ceil(rank);
  
  // Handle edge case where rank is exactly at the last index
  if (lowerIdx === n - 1) {
    return sorted[n - 1];
  }
  
  // Linear interpolation between closest ranks
  const fraction = rank - lowerIdx;
  return sorted[lowerIdx] + fraction * (sorted[upperIdx] - sorted[lowerIdx]);
}
```

```typescript
function windowsOf<T>(items: readonly T[], size: number): T[][] {
    if (size < 1) {
        throw new RangeError('size must be at least 1');
    }

    const length = items.length;
    if (length === 0 && size === 1) {
        return [];
    }

    if (length < size) {
        throw new RangeError('size must not be larger than the input length');
    }

    const windows = [];
    for (let i = 0; i <= length - size; i++) {
        const window: T[] = [];
        for (let j = 0; j < size; j++) {
            window.push(items[i + j]);
        }
        windows.push(window);
    }

    return windows;
}
```

```typescript
/**
 * Retrieves the value for an own key from an object.
 * Throws RangeError if the key is not an own property.
 */
export function deepGet<T, K extends keyof T>(
  source: T,
  key: K
): T[K] {
  if (!Object.hasOwn(source, key)) {
    throw new RangeError(`Property '${key}' is not an own property`);
  }
  return source[key];
}

/**
 * Extracts values from an array of objects using a specific key.
 * Returns undefined for items that do not have the key or are non-objects.
 * Uses inherited properties when available.
 */
export function pluck<T, K extends keyof T>(
  items: readonly T[],
  key: K
): T[K][] {
  return items.map(item => {
    if (typeof item !== 'object' || item === null) {
      return undefined;
    }
    return item[key];
  });
}
```

```typescript
function titleCase(text: string): string {
  // Handle empty or blank string
  if (!text || text.trim() === '') {
    return '';
  }

  // Trim leading and trailing whitespace
  const trimmed = text.trim();

  // Split by one or more whitespace characters
  const words = trimmed.split(/\s+/);

  // Process each word
  const result: string[] = [];

  for (const word of words) {
    if (word.length === 0) {
      result.push('');
      continue;
    }

    // Capitalize first letter, keep rest as-is but lowercase if it was uppercase
    const firstChar = word[0].toUpperCase();
    const rest = word.slice(1).toLowerCase();

    result.push(firstChar + rest);
  }

  // Join with single spaces
  return result.join(' ');
}
```

```typescript
  let slug = text.toLowerCase();

  }

  return slug;
}
```

```python
from collections import Counter

def top_words(text, k):
    if k <= 0:
        return []
    
    # Convert to lowercase
    text = text.lower()
    
    # Extract words: keep punctuation as part of the word, split by whitespace
    words = re.findall(r'\b\w+|[^\w\s]', text)

        return []

    counter = Counter(words)
    
    # Sort by frequency (descending), then alphabetically (ascending) for ties
    result = sorted(counter.items(), key=lambda x: (-x[1], x[0]))
    
    # Return top k words
    return [word for word, _ in result[:k]]
```

```python
        self.stack = []
        self.min_stack = []
```

```python
        self.stack.append(value)
        if not self.min_stack or value <= self.min_stack[-1]:
            self.min_stack.append(value)
    
    def pop(self):
        """Remove and return the top element. Raises ValueError if empty. O(1) time."""
        if not self.stack:
            raise ValueError("Pop from empty stack")
        value = self.stack.pop()
        if value == self.min_stack[-1]:
            self.min_stack.pop()
        return value
    
    def top(self):
        """Return the top element without removing it. Raises ValueError if empty. O(1) time."""
        if not self.stack:
            raise ValueError("Top from empty stack")
        return self.stack[-1]
    
    def minimum(self):
        """Return the minimum element in the stack. Raises ValueError if empty. O(1) time."""
        if not self.min_stack:
            raise ValueError("Minimum from empty stack")
```
